evals.name: ranked-multi-archetype-proposals
evals.setup: The project calls `must.Value` at 34 sites, 28 of them wrapped in the same three-line error-drop, and builds the same options struct inline at 12 more. The library is a local module under a `replace` directive, so its source is editable.
expected_behavior: Opens with the resolved library, the consumer scope, and the call-site count
Proposes across several archetypes, including at least one structural move — absorbing the repeated sequence, or moving a responsibility upstream — not only a rename or a single helper
Ranks by impact (reach × savings × quality, discounted by breakage and effort) and leads with the biggest win
Shows a real call site before → after for each proposal
Offers concrete diffs, since the library source is editable here

evals.name: proposals-stay-on-the-library
evals.setup: `oskit` is consumed across the module, but the run is scoped to `./pkg/render`. `oskit`'s source sits in the module cache with no `replace` and no `go.work` entry, so it is external. Several call sites could be tidied without touching `oskit` at all — the tempting wrong answer.
expected_behavior: Every proposal changes `oskit`'s API; the consumer diff is shown as the payoff, never as the proposal itself
Proposes no call-site-only refactor that leaves the API untouched
Proposed signatures follow the style Naming, Errors, and API design rules
Edits nothing — reports the proposal set and stops

evals.name: external-library-public-surface
evals.setup: `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` is an ordinary module dependency: no `replace`, no `go.work` entry, source in the module cache.
expected_behavior: Detects that the library is external and says so
Frames every proposal at the public-API level and notes it cannot diff internals
Offers a local wrapper as the fallback for changes that cannot land upstream

evals.name: terse-output
evals.setup: A run whose analysis would support eight proposals, capped at three.
expected_behavior: Opens with the one-line header and the ranked table — no preamble, no narration of mapping call sites
Reports at most three proposals, cutting from the bottom of the ranked list
Says in one line that the forced structural option was considered and what displaced it, if the cap evicted it — the cap hides nothing silently
States each proposal once, with no closing summary re-listing the table already shown

evals.name: restraint-on-an-api-that-is-fine
evals.setup: A small library the consumer uses cleanly: 9 call sites, no repeated wrapper, no inline config building, no re-declared interface, no error-string matching. Nothing about the consuming code is obviously improvable by changing the library.
expected_behavior: Says the API fits its consumer and proposes little or nothing, rather than manufacturing eight proposals to fill the default cap
Does not force a structural proposal into existence when no friction supports one — the forcing rule is about not stopping at renames, not a quota
Still reports the header line with the real call-site count, so the reader can see the analysis happened
